subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Don Quixote and the Birth of the Novel
description: A 60-second lesson on Don Quixote and the Birth of the Novel.

hook.text: In 1605, a broke Spanish tax collector wrote a book many scholars now call the first modern novel.

buildup.text: Don Quixote followed an aging man who read so many knight tales that he believed he was one himself.

discovery.text: Cervantes used the story to blur the line between fiction and reality in ways never done before.

twist.text: The book mocked chivalric romances so effectively that the entire genre collapsed across Europe.

climax.text: Don Quixote invented the unreliable narrator and self-aware fiction four centuries before postmodernism.

punchline.text: A madman on a horse invented the modern novel.

quiz.question: Why is Don Quixote considered groundbreaking?
options: It was the shortest book ever published
It blurred fiction and reality and is often called the first modern novel
It was the first book written in English
